summary: Harness optimization is often studied with a fixed policy model and benchmark. When either changes, the optimizer must decide which parts of an evolved harness to reuse or revise, but the harness alone may not explain why earlier edits were made or how they performed.
takeaways: In this work, we study Continual Recursive Self-Improvement (CRSI), a setting for continuing existing harness-optimization methods across compatible benchmarks or policy models.
We propose Self-Improvement Memory (SIM) for the harness optimizer, rather than the task-solving policy.
SIM groups edits by recurring harness problem and records their rationale, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation context.
